title: The emergency fund
objective: Size an emergency fund in months of expenses and decide where to hold it

q.prompt: Your car needs **$1,400** of repairs to get you to work tomorrow, and you have no savings. What usually happens next?

options.text: It goes on a credit card or loan, and you pay interest on it
Nothing: the garage waits until you're ready
options.why: Most garages want payment when the job's done.
That can cost more than the repair. Most people borrow instead.

q.explanation: Without a buffer, surprises become debt. An emergency fund turns a crisis into an inconvenience.

q.prompt: Guess: how many months of **essential** expenses does a common rule of thumb say to keep in an emergency fund?
q.explanation: A common starting rule is about 3 months of essentials, and up to 6 if your income is irregular or others rely on you.

screens.title: Cash for real surprises
screens.body: An [[emergency fund]] is money set aside for things you can't plan: losing your job, an urgent repair, a medical bill. It's not for holidays or sales. Size it in months of **essential** expenses: about 3 months is a common start, closer to 6 if your income is irregular.

visual.label: of essential expenses: a common rule of thumb

screens.title: Where to keep it
screens.body: Somewhere **separate**, **safe** and **quick to reach**: usually a savings account apart from your everyday one. Deposits at Australian banks are protected by the [[Financial Claims Scheme]] up to {{fcsLimit}} per person per bank. Shares can drop just when you need the cash.

screens.title: Worked example: Chloe, Melbourne
screens.body: Chloe's essential costs are rent, groceries, bills and transport.

lines: First milestone: $1,000, so small shocks are covered sooner

q.prompt: Is this a job for the emergency fund?
q.hint: Ask: is it unexpected and necessary, or just a good deal?
q.explanation: Emergencies are unexpected and necessary. Deals and treats belong in their own savings goals.

q.prompt: Jai's essentials cost $2,200 a month. What's a 3-month emergency fund target?
q.hint: Multiply monthly essentials by the number of months.

q.prompt: Where is the best place for Jai's emergency fund?

options.text: A separate savings account at an Australian bank

options.why: Share prices can fall just when you need the money, like during a downturn when jobs are lost.

options.text: His everyday account, so it's easy to reach
options.why: Mixed with spending money, it tends to get spent.

q.hint: You want it safe, separate, and available within a day.
q.explanation: A separate savings account keeps it out of daily spending, earns interest and is covered by the Financial Claims Scheme.

q.sentence: Size your emergency fund using your ___ expenses, not everything you spend.
q.explanation: In a real emergency you'd cut wants, so only essentials need covering.

q.prompt: Ravi is a freelance designer with irregular income. His essentials are $3,100 a month and he wants 6 months covered. What's his target?
q.explanation: $3,100 × 6 = $18,600. Irregular income is a good reason to aim for the bigger buffer.

q.prompt: Your target is $6,000 and you can save $150 a week. How many weeks will it take?
q.explanation: $6,000 ÷ $150 = 40 weeks, a bit under a year.

q.prompt: In a 50/30/20 budget, which bucket should regular emergency fund deposits come from?

options.text: The 20% for savings and extra debt

options.why: Needs are today's essentials. The fund is saving for later.
It's not a treat; it's protection, so it belongs with savings.

q.explanation: Building a buffer is saving, so it comes from the 20% bucket.

screens.title: Set your number
screens.body: Add up one month of your essentials: rent, groceries, bills, transport. Multiply by 3. That's your target. If you don't have a separate savings account, opening one takes minutes in most banking apps.
screens.action: Work out your **3-month emergency fund target**.

bullets: An emergency fund covers real surprises, so they don't become debt.
Aim for about 3 months of essentials; 6 if income is irregular.
Keep it in a separate, protected savings account, not shares.

reviewBank.prompt: Essentials are $2,500 a month. What's a 3-month emergency fund?
Shares are a good place for an emergency fund because they grow faster than savings.
reviewBank.explanation: Shares can fall when you need the money. Emergency cash needs to be safe and available.

reviewBank.prompt: Which is a true emergency-fund expense?

options.why: Planned events need their own savings goal.

reviewBank.explanation: Unexpected and necessary costs, like urgent dental work, are what the fund is for.

reviewBank.prompt: Without an emergency fund, a surprise bill often ends up as debt.
reviewBank.explanation: With no buffer, people usually reach for a card or loan, and pay interest.
